An assumed stair that is cut off is read the other way at build (the plan of the level above names its half landing; architect K4, the action flip_stair), and the model review's M9 reports every stair, door or floor part no walk reaches, so Argus sees it before the user does.

lessons.request: A throw or any cloth never shows its host through it: a cloth sunk into its host deeper than its own thickness is no rest (not built, reported)
lessons.lesson: A cloth (a throw) is measured with its own S5 tolerance (rest.REST_TOLERANCES decor_pen_cloth_m 7 mm, under its 8 mm thickness): sunk deeper, the host shows through it and it is not built (not rested, reported); a cushion keeps the soft 3 cm.

lessons.request: Give the agent loop and the big improvement loop time in every run: the regular agent rounds leave the big loop its first measure and a cycle; pod runs may take up to 180 min
lessons.lesson: AgentLoop.reserve_s (scheduler.big_loop_reserve): the regular rounds leave the big loop its first measure (10 min) and one cycle (a final round's share of the final stages + 10 min of looks); the big loop takes what is left, up to 4 cycles. Pod runs up to 180 min with --over-5-ok (user OK of 27 Oct 2026).

lessons.request: clashing sink and bath, also bath is not in proper place: drawn sanitary ware never stands in another drawn fixture; a bath read as a merged outline (bath, screen, vanity edge) is seated as a real product on its wall beside the basin, not turned across the room

An outline outside its type's sizes is misread or merged (a corner bath read with its screen and the vanity's edge): neither its centre nor its box angle is the piece's, so the real product is seated in it, its back on a wall and along it, covering most of the outline, clear of the other drawn fixtures and the door swings, a corner counting more. Two drawn fixtures that cut each other: the weaker reading gives way, sliding along its wall (at most 0.5 m), else seated in its drawn outline. The reading (ai_named_members, fix_fixed), the build's clash resolver (F5, the fitted model follows a new size), the architect's move_piece and Argus (a code decision from every clash left) apply it.

lessons.request: correct the door (real06's entrance at the top of the outside steps: a narrow oak strip with a dark panel beside it in the opening). General rule: a library door or window fills its opening as a real product does: the catalogue box is read in the piece frame it is written in; a door or window model deeper than wide has its front along its leaf and is turned to its leaf's face; the build refuses a fit that stretches a model's width and height by very different factors; a one-leaf door takes no model wider than a real leaf (1.25 m) and none named as a pair or a sliding system: a wider entrance gets the parametric leaf with glazed side lights or a pair (D5); leaf and frame centred in the opening
lessons.lesson: A library door or window fills its opening as a real product does: its catalogue box is read in the piece frame it is written in; a door or window model deeper than wide has its front along its leaf and is turned to its leaf's face; a fit that stretches a model's width and height by very different factors is refused (the parametric opening instead); a one-leaf door takes no model wider than a real leaf (1.25 m) nor one named as a pair or a sliding system (a wider entrance gets the leaf with glazed side lights, or D5's pair); the leaf and its frame stand centred in the opening.
lessons.question: Does every outside door fill its opening as a real door: one leaf of a real width (side lights or a pair when wider), centred, never turned or stretched?

lessons.request: doors next to each other not making sense (real06's dressing room and upper hall: the AI made the windows beside the doors of two rooms doors, three doors side by side). General rule: no two doors whose openings overlap or whose frames touch (less than two frames of wall between them, or frames meeting at a corner), no two doors between the same two rooms closer than a door's width, no two swing leaves into one room that sweep over each other; a window becomes a door only for a room no door reaches and never beside the door of two rooms; the model review (M12) finds it in every project, a decision that makes it worse is refused, Argus revokes the AI decision that made such a door, and two drawn doors of one passage whose frames touch become one opening (O1)
lessons.lesson: Doors never crowd each other: no two doors whose openings overlap or whose frames touch (two frames of wall between them, none meeting at a corner), no two doors between the same two rooms closer than a door's width, no two leaves that sweep over each other; a window becomes a door only for a room no door reaches, never beside the door of two rooms; the model review (M12) finds it in every project, Argus revokes the AI decision that made such a door, two drawn doors of one passage whose frames touch become one opening (O1).
lessons.question: Does any door stand against another door (touching frames, one passage drawn twice, leaves that hit each other)?

lessons.request: Not every opening inside the house requires a door or a window. General rule: an opening between two rooms drawn with no leaf and no swing arc (a passage, an archway, an open doorway between a hall and a dressing room, a kitchen and a living area) stays an open passage: no leaf, no glass, no guard (a guard only over a drop); where the drawing is unclear the open passage is the default, a door (one solid leaf) only into a room that needs privacy (a bathroom, a WC, a bedroom); a door or passage between rooms is never made a window, a serving hatch over a drawn counter is open (no glass); the architect logs the decision (D6) and the model review (M12) reports an inside opening that got a leaf, glass or a guard it does not need
lessons.lesson: Not every opening inside the house has a door or a window: a passage between two rooms drawn with no leaf and no swing arc stays open (no leaf, no glass, no guard: a guard only over a drop); where the drawing is unclear the open passage is the default and a door (one solid leaf) goes only into a room that needs privacy (a bathroom, a WC, a bedroom); a door or passage between rooms is never made a window, a serving hatch over a drawn counter stays open; D6 logs the decision and the model review (M12) reports an inside opening that got a leaf, glass or a guard it does not need.
lessons.question: Does every opening inside the house get only what it needs: an open passage where none is drawn, a door only for privacy?

lessons.request: Tall windows where the style favours large glazing (user, 27 Oct 2026, on a Scandinavian two-storey house's renders: 'In some of the rooms the full windows from top to bottom (with a bit of remaining wall of course) could look better').
lessons.lesson: In a style family that favours large glazing (scandinavian, japandi, modern, minimal, contemporary; not classic, rustic, mediterranean, industrial) the windows of the living, dining and bed rooms (and of a dry room onto a terrace or garden) whose sill and head no document fixes become tall windows: a 0.20 m upstand to 0.25 m under the ceiling or the roof, the drawn width and position kept, all windows of one facade of the room alike; never in a wet room, never behind a wall-backed piece (a dresser, wardrobe, bed head, desk, sideboard or kitchen run keeps the sill the fit caps it at); the house's guard over a drop (W3); curtains and blinds follow the new head (architect rule W5, action tall_window).
lessons.question: Do the living, dining and bed rooms of a large-glazing style have tall windows wherever the documents fix no sill or head and no wall-backed piece stands in front, the same on every facade of the room, with a guard over a drop?

lessons.request: Roofs and columns of outdoor spaces (user, 28 Oct 2026, on real06's balcony facade: 'There is no column supporting the roof also columns under is too thick, no sloped roof next to the balcony').
lessons.lesson: A drawn column is built in the size of its own outline on the column layer (the circle or box on KOLON/COLUMN), never of its hatch and axis cross. Where the building's drawn roof covers an outdoor space and reaches more than 1.5 m out from the walls over a corner, that corner gets a post from the space's floor to the eaves, continuing a drawn column below it. A lower roof the roof plan draws over a space is built as drawn: its outline, sloping away from the house at the house roof's pitch (at least 10 degrees, lowered to keep the clear height), covered like the house roof; only when no slope fits does the space get a light roof.

lessons.request: Entrances lead to doors (user, 28 Oct 2026, on real06's aerial view: 'Enterence to the window?').
lessons.lesson: Steps, paths, handrails and canopies belong to doors only: when any rule turns a door into a window (the architect, the furniture-in-front rule), its site entrance goes with it (site.entrances_removed), the build ignores an entrance whose opening is no door, and the door-widening rule never widens a window.

lessons.request: Nothing closes a full-height window (user, 28 Oct 2026, on real06's child's room: 'If this is a full window this thing here closing the window').
lessons.lesson: A wall-backed piece (dresser, sideboard, wardrobe, desk ...) cleared from a window slides along its own wall or stays; it is never pulled out into the room. Storage before a tall window blocks it whatever share it covers (G12), and a tall window (W5) keeps its sill where such a piece stands.

lessons.request: Doors open as drawn (user, 28 Oct 2026, on real06's living room: 'This window / door should have been sliding as indicated in the plan why it has been missed?').
lessons.lesson: A door or window model opens as the drawing and the architect's door kind say: a sliding opening gets a sliding model (a title naming folding, bi-fold, French or pivot is refused), else the parametric glazed sliding door.

lessons.request: Seats face the room (user, 28 Oct 2026, on real06's master bedroom: 'Why this chair looking at the wall').
lessons.lesson: Every drawn piece of a type with a front gets one: the side away from its only wall or towards its partner, else for a seat the quarter turn that looks into the most open floor towards its partner; a seat never looks at a wall.

lessons.request: Top-down views with every run (user, 28 Oct 2026: 'Where are the top down views of the last 2 runs give me real04 and real06').
lessons.lesson:
Every run's top-down views of each floor (renders/

/top__plan.jpg) are kept with the run: collected, promoted into results/baseline/latest, and sent with the review.

lessons.request: Skirting all around (user, 28 Oct 2026: 'baseboard needs to be all around').
lessons.lesson: The skirting runs all around every dry room's walls, cut only at doors, openings and low windows, up to the door casings and into the corners; an end that stops short of a corner or a casing is a finding; at an outside corner of the room (a wall nib, a pilaster, a wall end) both boards run on by their thickness and meet around it (shell.skirting_reflex_corners).
lessons.question: Does the skirting run all around every dry room's walls, up to the door casings and into the corners, with no gap?

lessons.request: This should not supposed to be 1 to one with what is under, it is a veranda this roof of veranda needs to make sense
lessons.lesson: A veranda or porch roof is designed, not traced: its outline fills the floor's notches, is the rectangle around the floor when that adds at most 15 % (a lean-to is a rectangle), reaches 0.25 m past the posts on its open sides and stops flush at the house (its small wall jogs do not cut it); posts stand inside the floor at its corners; its top is a roofing (standing seam in the frames' colour, or the house roof's tiles on a drawn lower roof), never the facade cladding or a deck look.
lessons.question: Does every outdoor roof read as a designed roof (a simple shape with eaves past the posts and a roofing on top), not a copy of the floor below?

lessons.request: I want better doors inside the house and the outside, I am not liking that much the models used at the moment, some variation is needed
lessons.lesson: Doors inside and outside are good-looking real products with variation by role in one language: a statement entrance door, glazed terrace doors, interior doors in the style (flush, panelled or glazed by room: glazed or framed glass to living rooms and kitchens, solid to bedrooms and bathrooms, sliding or pocket where drawn), with handles and frames; never one plain model everywhere. The build picks the audit's best-rated library models (the HSSD door and window series beside the 3D Warehouse ones): the entrance a statement door, the outside service doors another family than the entrance, the terrace doors glazed, one window family, and among equally good families the house's own pick (two houses of one style differ); the interior doors one family per room role, never a facade family, facing the room they open into, the parametric door where no model fits (opening_models.plan, plan_inside); Argus finds every door one model, an inside door model on the facade and an entrance without a statement door (opening_models.door_variety_problems).
lessons.question: Do the doors look like chosen products, with a distinct entrance door and interior doors that vary by room in one style?

lessons.request: also more stylish internal walls please better color and for the baths and kitchen better desings
lessons.lesson: Interior walls are styled: a palette per style with warm whites and one accent per room (a feature wall behind a bed or sofa, panelling, wallpaper or limewash where the style allows); bathrooms and kitchens are designed rooms (tiled walls to the right height, a vanity with mirror and light, a real bath or shower set; a kitchen run with wall units, splashback, appliances and worktop decor).
lessons.question: Do the interior walls carry a colour scheme of the style, and are the bathrooms and kitchens designed like magazine rooms?

lessons.request: All these feedback needs to be understand by argus an Argus needs to be able to make these kind of corrections in the future projects
lessons.lesson: Argus learns every user lesson: each lesson's question is asked on every run (Argus AI's walk on the top-down views and renders, the inspector's checks) and, where code can measure it, an Argus line finds the problem by itself and routes it to the fix that removes it (an architect action, an agent tool, a rerun or the rule to write).
lessons.question: Did Argus ask every user lesson's question on this run and fix what it found?

lessons.request: Mirrors in the baths is missing sometimes
lessons.lesson: Every built basin has a mirror over it, a required item, not an AI option: above it, else on the nearest free wall beside it (within 1.2 m, 0.6 m wide, slid towards the basin) when a window is behind it; an inferred basin gets one too.
lessons.question: Does every basin have a mirror over or beside it?

lessons.request: There should have been better indoor stair solutions should be there I did not like this one
lessons.lesson: A U stair that needs winders turns them as two quarter turns of kite winders around the newels at its well (never one fan of treads from a single point); handrails and balustrade follow the house style.
lessons.question: Do the stairs read as designed stairs (clean flights, winders turning around the newels, a continuous handrail), not a spiral fan or a heavy block?

lessons.request: Kitchen design could have been a lot better this is terrible (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, kitchen r_L-1_mutfak: the drawn stove got a freestanding white cooker lower than the worktop standing in a gap of the run like a dishwasher, no cooker hood, wall cabinets as separate boxes of odd widths with gaps that do not line up; real06 run 20261027-222248-full: 'What kind of a kitchen is this', 'Why is this closing the window': wall cabinets across a window, the hob a black freestanding box between base units)
lessons.lesson: A kitchen reads as one designed kitchen (general rule): a stove drawn in a counter run is the run's hob, set into one continuous worktop at its drawn span with a built-in oven under it (a freestanding range only away from a run); an agent pin never takes a hob or a fridge out of its run; every hob gets a cooker hood sized to it in the style's metal (a chimney hood on the wall, an under-cabinet hood under a wall cabinet, an island hood over an island); the wall cabinets are one run over the base run: one bottom and top line, one depth, real units of 300-900 mm whose joints line up with the base units, flush at the hood (the hood between them), never over any part of a window, a glazed door or a door (the build cuts them at the windows of the building as built), joined at the corners (a blind corner unit, a corner filler), never a lone box of odd width; a counter outline drawn inside a run is part of it; a fridge column never stands in front of a window or a pass-through; fronts, handles (on feet) and the worktop follow the style, the family's kitchen look where style.json names none. The model review's M13 flags what is left (a hob without a hood, an appliance off the worktop line, wall cabinets over a window, odd boxes, unexplained gaps, two lines) for Argus.
lessons.question: Does every kitchen read as one designed kitchen: the hob set into the worktop with an oven under it and a hood over it, every appliance of a run on its worktop line, the wall cabinets one run of real units in line with the base units, flush at the hood, joined at the corners and never over a window?

lessons.request: More decor pieces needed ... kettle in the kitchen, microwave in the kitchen etc (real06's kitchen: nothing on the counter)
lessons.lesson: Every kitchen's worktop is dressed modestly by rule (general rule): a countertop microwave at a run end against a wall or a corner, a coffee machine (or a toaster) at another end, a kettle by the sink, a utensil pot and a chopping board beside the hob, a fruit bowl on an island or a free stretch, at real product sizes (parametric with PBR materials until audited library models exist), at most one per 0.5 m of free worktop and five per kitchen, labelled added_by_ai with the reason; each passes the code checks: on the worktop (rested on the built top), off the hob and its 0.25 m side gap, off the sink, off tall units, never in front of a window, glazed door or pass-through it would reach (the build slides it along the worktop when the building as built puts a window there).
lessons.question: Does every kitchen worktop carry a few real small appliances and pieces of decor (a microwave, a kettle, a coffee machine or toaster, a board, a fruit bowl), none on the hob, in the sink or in front of a window?

lessons.request: still flying pillows all around (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, the upper-floor living room's two sofas: the cushions stood at the seat's front edge, some 0.3 m in front of the backrest, with a gap under them)
lessons.lesson: A decor cushion on a sofa or an armchair rests on the seat and leans on the backrest: it touches its back in its upper part (S5 measure_back, decor_back_gap_m 1.5 cm) and its seat under it. The back rays run at least 4 cm over the seat and a hit on the seat's own dome or front lip (a face looking up, or something rising less than 0.15 m over the seat) is never the back; the frame's 12 degrees is the least lean, the cushion leans at the styled 20 degrees, further when nothing is behind its upper part, and slides onto its back (rest.plan_decor, settle_back). One that cannot rest so is not built and reported, never left floating.
lessons.question: Does every cushion on a sofa or an armchair sit on the seat and lean on the backrest?

lessons.request: I did not like this bed (real04 f_L0_021: a cream decor throw draped over a bed model that has its own made bedding; the model's grey blanket poked through it in dark patches and the drape tore over its folds)
lessons.lesson: No decor throw on a bed whose model is already made up with its own duvet or cover (the audit's has_bedding: decor.takes_throw in the decor stage, rest.own_bedding at the build). Any throw is built only where its drape stays clear: nothing of the host pokes through the cloth between its grid points (decor_cloth_poke_m) and the drape does not tear (decor_cloth_edge_m); else it is not built and reported (S5, model review M14).
lessons.question: Does every bed with its own bedding stay without a second cloth over it, and does every throw lie clean on its host?

lessons.request: flying pillows (real04 cam_r_L0_e_yatak_odasi_1, bed f_L0_007 dressed with our duvet and pillows: the two decor cushions stood upright in front of the bed's pillows with no contact with the pillows behind or the mattress below)
lessons.lesson: On a bed our build dresses (a duvet and lying pillows) a decor cushion first stands on the pillows against the headboard (the back rays see the bed alone), else it leans back on the pillows (the bed and its pillows), never on the duvet's fold; its seat and its S5 check are measured on the bedding as built, the duvet included (furniture.BED_CASTER / LEAN_CASTER, rest.plan_decor back_caster). It touches what is behind it in its upper part, or it is not built.
lessons.question: Does every decor cushion on a bed rest on the pillows or the mattress and lean on the pillows or the headboard?

lessons.request: Light is flying in the air needs to be connected to ceiling (real04 r_L-1_salon: the dining pendant over the long table hung 0.99 m under the ceiling with no cord, rod or canopy)
lessons.lesson: Every pendant and ceiling light is connected to the ceiling over it (the sloped ceiling too): a ceiling light sits flush; a pendant whose own top is at most 10 cm under the ceiling is lifted to it; a pendant further down keeps its shade where the decor stage put it and gets a cord and a ceiling canopy from its top to the ceiling (furniture.hang_plan, parametric.suspension_parts). The scene check S5 (hang_gap) and the model review M14 flag a hung piece whose top is more than 2 cm under the ceiling with nothing bridging the gap.
lessons.question: Does every hanging light reach the ceiling with a cord or rod and a canopy?

lessons.request: More flying pillows (real04 cam_r_L0_e_yatak_odasi_3, the same bed f_L0_007: the decor cushions stood up in front of the bed's pillows with gaps under and behind them)
lessons.lesson: A floating cushion is caught before the user sees it: S5 measures the gap behind a leaning item's upper part (measure_back) as well as under it, the model review M14 re-judges every decor rest record, and Argus files both under the problem kind 'detached' (a piece not attached to what holds it), so a recurring float gets counted in the problem log; a fix is checked on every view of the piece, not one.
lessons.question: Is any decor item detached from what holds it (S5, M14)?

lessons.request: More decor pieces needed, plates on tables for example
lessons.lesson: Tops are styled, not bare: every dining table is set at each chair (a plate in front of it, a glass at the diner's right) with a centre bowl when its middle is free; coffee tables, sideboards, consoles, dressers and TV units carry a small group (up to three: books, a tray, a vase, a bowl), nightstands, side tables and desks up to two small pieces, bookshelves a vase and a candle on their boards (wenart.furniture.tabletop). Each piece rests on the real top by rays (S5), keeps clear of the others, is added_by_ai with its reason, and the brief's decor switch turns it off; kitchen appliances are the kitchen's.
lessons.question: Is every dining table set and every top styled with a few pieces resting on it?

lessons.request: what is this miniature table makes no sense (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, cam_r_L-1_salon_3: the drawn coffee table f_L-1_087 got the 3D Warehouse model 'Facit High Table W2400 D800 mm NamNam Barstool Low back Metal Leg', a 2.4 m high table with its barstools in one mesh whose box was read in feet so that it passed as a 0.73 m coffee table). General rule: a model whose title states its size is used only when the size agrees with its box (a unit factor corrects it or it is refused), and a model whose title names a set of pieces is never one piece
lessons.lesson: A library model is used only when its own names agree with it: a title that states its size (W2400 D800 mm, 120 x 60 x 36 cm, 34"h x 30"w) must match its box, a unit factor (feet, inches, cm, mm, x10, x100) that explains the mismatch corrects it only when the corrected box is a real piece of the type, else the model is refused; a title naming the pieces of a group (a table with chairs, stools or barstools, a chair with an ottoman, a sofa with an armchair, a bed with nightstands, a toilet with a basin, a dining or bistro set) is a set and never one piece (wenart/furniture/model_title.py: catalog.usable, the audit's model_title check, python -m wenart.assets audit title-rules, the fit report and the code critic's LT, Argus P11).
lessons.question: Does every built library model's stated size agree with its box, and does its title name one piece of its type?

lessons.request: This makes no sense and terrible sink / Terrible sink (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, cam_r_L0_e_banyo_1 and cam_r_L-1_banyo_1: five washbasins got the 3D Warehouse model 'Sink' from the zip's Kitchen folder, a double-bowl kitchen sink with a drainboard hung on the wall with a strap mirror above it). General rule: a washbasin is a bathroom basin (its names or its source say so); a model titled only 'sink' or naming a kitchen, a drainer or a double bowl is a kitchen sink, never a washbasin; a title of another type than the catalogue type refuses the model
lessons.lesson: A washbasin is a bathroom basin: its names or its source say so (basin, washbasin, lavatory, vanity, bathroom sink, lavabo, Waschbecken, wastafel; the source's Bathroom folder; HSSD found_in bathroom); a model titled only 'sink' or naming a kitchen, a drainer or drainboard, a double bowl or a commercial sink is a kitchen sink and never a washbasin, a kitchen sink named for a bathroom is no kitchen sink, and every model whose title names another type (or whose title and vision check both name another type) is refused for its catalogue type (model_title title_type; the same checks as above).
lessons.question: Is every washbasin a bathroom basin, never a kitchen sink, and every model the type its title names?

lessons.request: is this a window? how is this making sense? (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, L0 top view between r_L0_yatak_odasi and r_L0_e_yatak_odasi: the drawn wardrobe f_L0_023 got the 3D Warehouse model 'WARDROBE' whose 0.64 m end shows a white two-pane glazed frame; the vision audit said is_type false and size_plausible false, the geometry put the detail on that end, the audit turned its front to the long face and kept it as fix). General rule: a model the vision audit doubts (not its type, an odd size) is not used until a later audit pass confirms it; a front turned off its detail side gets a second look; a window or glazed frame on furniture is a wrong object (D2) and is swapped
lessons.lesson: A model the vision audit said is not its type, or whose size it found odd, is not used until a second audit pass confirms its type (audit.status pending; decide.second_look, pass 2 asks it; two passes against it remove it); a model of a long-front type whose detailed face is an end while the audit turned its front to the long face gets a second look (pending): an end with a glazed panel or a window is no wardrobe front; the vision critics treat a window or a glazed frame on a piece of furniture as a wrong object (D2, swap_model) and no swap or pin takes a model the audit or its names refuse.
lessons.question: Does any piece of furniture show a window, a glazed frame or another object that is not its type?

lessons.request: What kind of a bath is this / this bath needs to make sense (real06 run 20261027-222248-full: both bathtubs f_L0_010 and f_L1_009 got the 3D Warehouse model 'Bathtub', 1.52 x 0.74 x 0.37 m, 85 % non-manifold edges, the vision answer real_product false, size_plausible false, quality 2, audited keep). General rule: a furniture model rated 2 or lower or found no real product is not used, a fixture is fitted only at its real height (a bath's rim 0.45-0.65 m), and the bath built from code looks like a real product (rim, taps, a panel when it stands in a niche between walls)
lessons.lesson: A furniture model the vision audit rated 2 or lower, or found no real product, is not used (removed; decor keeps the doubt), and a fixture is fitted only at its real height without tolerance (a bath's top 0.45-0.65 m: fit.FIXTURE_HEIGHTS; the washbasin's working top: fit.WORKING_TOPS); when no model is left the bath is built from code as a real product: a ceramic shell with a flat rim, the bowl floor with a drain and an overflow, a chrome deck mixer at the end on a wall, and a panel under a rim band on every open side when its back stands on a wall (a niche: the front panel; a corner: the front and the open end; fixture_seat.bath_walls).
lessons.question: Does every bath stand at a real rim height (0.45-0.65 m) and look like a real product, with its taps and its panel where it stands between walls?

lessons.request: There could be better outside solutions to the grade slope (real04 run 20261028-005318-full: on the slope between the pool terrace and the garden, bare concrete box planters stacked like stairs, steps cutting through boxes, a tilted paved ramp running diagonally down the slope with a strip of lawn inside it, grey retaining walls)
lessons.lesson: A level difference in the garden is designed as a landscape architect builds it, on every project: where the ground can be graded (room inside the plot, clear of the house and the other platforms, a way past left, a natural slope gentler than the bank) the terrace meets the ground by a lawn bank of at most 1:3 or a planted bank of at most 1:2, no wall; a taller difference steps down in terraces whose tiers along one side share one level, each tier a planted bed, every tier end walled; steps are real flights (risers of at most 0.15 m, the step rule, a landing every 12 risers) that follow the ground to their foot, with cheek walls and a landing, and the terraces stop beside them (no steps through a planter); a path is laid level across, up to 1:20 a walk with an edging, up to 1:12 a sloped walk, steeper a stepped path of landings and short flights with stone step edges and a handrail over 0.45 m; a ramp only on an accessible route; retaining walls in the house's base stone with a coping (wenart/blender/grading.py; the model review's M15 and the architect's G2 check it)
lessons.question: Does the garden meet every level difference as a landscape architect would build it: banks of at most 1:3 / 1:2, terraces at one level per side and planted, flights of solid treads with cheek walls and a landing, paths level across and stepped where steeper than 1:12, a ramp only where accessibility asks, walls in the house's base stone with a coping?

lessons.request: Better solutions needed for the elevation difference outside (an aerial view of real04: a bare grey concrete retaining wall box next to the paved terrace and the pool, inside it a row of loose concrete bars or slabs lying across the grass like floating step treads, with grass between them)
lessons.lesson: Never a loose tread or slab over the grass and never a bare concrete box: every step of a garden flight is a solid block on the one below and on the ground, from the upper level to the lower one, its flight a hole in the lawn held by cheek walls that stand over the ground beside it, its last riser landing on a landing pad at the highest ground under it (a flight that would end under the lawn is not built: the edge meets the ground); a level difference is a planted slope (at most 1:3 lawn, 1:2 ground cover), terraced planters with a coping and planting, or such steps; every retaining, cheek and wing wall has a finish (the house's base stone) and a coping; the model review's M15 G2 / G6 and the architect's G2 find a tread that does not sit on its riser or the ground and a bare concrete or uncoped wall
lessons.question: Does every garden step sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and is every retaining wall finished in stone or render with a coping (never bare concrete)?

lessons.request: I am not liking this is the only outside flooring (real06 / real04: the garden path and the entrance steps in the same large grey square slabs with mossy joints as the terraces and the drive, with steel handrails)
lessons.lesson: The outdoor floors are a designed set by use and style family, never one slab everywhere: the terrace and pool deck in stone or porcelain slabs with a tight joint (decking where the style calls for it), the steps and copings in a stone with a tread edge, the garden path in gravel, clay or brick pavers with a stone edging where it meets the lawn, the drive and parking in a stronger paver, all in one language with the house's base stone; a material the documents draw, or a paving the style or the brief names for the terrace, wins; every inferred floor is recorded with its reason (grading.floor_set; the model review's M15 G7 and the architect's G3 find a site whose every outdoor floor has one look)
lessons.question: Does each outdoor floor have the material of its use (terrace and pool deck, steps, garden path, drive), in one language with the house's base, never one slab everywhere?

lessons.request: makes no sense to have that table with the carpet outside, that's outside area (real04 run 20261028-005318-full, the roof terrace r_L1_teras: an indoor turned-leg pine dining table, two indoor dining chairs and a wool runner rug on the paving). General rule: an outdoor room (balcony, terrace, roof terrace, loggia, veranda, patio, any room open to the sky) and every outdoor space of the site takes no rug, runner or other indoor textile on its floor; its furniture is outdoor furniture: the fit takes only library models made for outside (named for outside or of an outdoor material such as teak, rattan, wicker, resin; never one named for inside, material tags alone do not count), else the parametric family in weather-proof materials (a steel frame with teak), recorded as a library gap; the model review (M16) and Argus find an indoor rug or an indoor model outside in every project
lessons.lesson: An outdoor room (balcony, terrace, roof terrace, loggia, veranda, patio, any room open to the sky) and every outdoor space of the site is dressed for outside: no rug, runner or other indoor textile on its floor (no rug slot, no solver rug, no outdoor-set rug; any laid by a later rule is taken out); its tables, chairs, benches and seats are outdoor furniture: the fit takes only library models made for outside (named for outside, or of an outdoor material such as teak, rattan, wicker or resin; never one named for inside; material tags alone do not count), else the parametric family in weather-proof materials (a steel frame with teak), recorded as a library gap; the architect (U1), the model review (M16) and Argus find an indoor rug or an indoor model outside in every project.
lessons.question: Is every outdoor room and outdoor space dressed for outside: no rug or carpet on its floor, and only furniture made for outside (no indoor table, no upholstered indoor chair)?

lessons.request: More lights from the ceiling needed (real04 run 20261028-005318-full: the 50.9 m2 living and dining room had one pendant over its 3.35 m table, the bedrooms one light, the halls none). General rule: every room gets the ceiling lights of its functional zones (a row of pendants along each dining table and kitchen island by its length, a light over each seating group, bed, desk and counter run) and enough general light for its floor by the lumen method (N = E x A / (F x UF x MF), the illuminance per room type scaled by the style's decor density), spread evenly, never over a wall cabinet, a tall cabinet or a stair, never in a door swing, mounted on the slope under a sloped ceiling with its lowest point 2.0 m over the floor; the model review (M17) and Argus flag a room with too little ceiling light
lessons.lesson: Every room gets the ceiling lights of its functional zones (a row of pendants along each dining table and kitchen island by its length, a light over each seating group, bed, desk and kitchen counter run) and enough general light for its floor by the lumen method (N = E x A / (F x UF x MF): a designer illuminance per room type scaled by the style's decor density, 1100 lm lamps), spread evenly; never over a wall cabinet, a tall cabinet, a wardrobe, a counter or a stair, never in a door swing; under a sloped ceiling a flush light is mounted on the slope with its lowest point 2.0 m over the floor; the decor stage hangs them whatever the AI chose (decor.ceiling_lights), the model review (M17) and Argus flag a room with too little ceiling light.
lessons.question: Does every room have enough ceiling light for its size and its groups: pendants along the dining table, a light over the seating, the bed, the desk and the kitchen run, and an even general light?
